chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhayna, from al-Fadl ibn Yasar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The people say that the Qur'an came down upon seven Ahruf.' He said: 'The enemies of Allah have lied! Rather, it came down upon one Harf from the One.'

key_terms.الْوَاحِدِ: Al-Wahid (The One, referring to God's unity)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the number of Ahruf the Qur'an was revealed in?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) refutes the claim that the Qur'an was revealed in seven different 'Ahruf' (modes/variants), asserting instead that it came down as a single, unified 'Harf' from the One God. This narration emphasizes the unity and singular origin of the Qur'anic text against the concept of multiple variant readings. In Shia scholarship, this is often interpreted to mean that while the Qur'an possesses internal flexibility (such as in recitation styles or legal implications), its core revelation is singular and unchanging, preserving its divine integrity.

en.ammaar-muslim: [1563/2] al-Kafi: Ali b. Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Umar b. Udhayna from al-Fudhayl b. Yasar who said:

I said to Abi Abdillah عليه السلام: The people say that the Qur’an came down upon seven Ahruf? So he (i.e. the Imam) said: The enemies of Allah have lied! Rather it came down upon one Harf from the One
